fixture_notes.purpose: coverage-validation case: a small Express web application whose package.json declares 25 directly classified npm packages (coverage_plan) across three groups, used to measure recall and false-positive rates against an independently obtained ground truth
fixture_notes.package_selection: express alone pulls roughly fifty of its own transitive dependencies on a standard npm install; those are additional, genuinely-used inventory this case does not itemize one by one, following the design note that express's own dependency tree is not trimmed to fit a round number. The 25 packages named in coverage_plan are each a direct package.json dependency chosen for its group, independent of express's own tree
fixture_notes.base_image: node:22-bookworm-slim (Debian-based, not Alpine), so the OS package family matches the Debian-based Python and Java cases
fixture_notes.startup_vs_lazy: the startup group is required at module load, before the firing signal; the lazy group is required only inside route handlers, which this program calls against its own local server once fired
fixture_notes.operational_processing: a background shell loop execs curl, git and openssl every five seconds once the container starts, independently of the firing signal, as this case's short-lived OS-package activity
fixture_notes.runtime_introspection: before exiting (or a fixed time after firing) the process appends one JSON Lines record per require.cache key to /var/log/runtime-modules.jsonl — the ground-truth tool's own independent source
fixture_notes.coverage_plan_caveat: the three groups are the fixture's design intent (GT-A), not the measured ground truth
